intro:
Use it to name an icon button, to show the keys for an action, or to add a line about a control that its label has no room for.

A tooltip only appears to a pointer or to keyboard focus. It cannot be opened on a touch screen, so put nothing in it that somebody needs in order to use the page, and nothing that can be pressed. For content with links or buttons, use a popover; for a message that must be read, an [Alert](/docs/web/components/alert).

Put one `Tooltip.Provider` round a group of tooltips, or round the whole app. The first tooltip waits half a second, so passing over a toolbar does not flash one at every button. Once one is open, the next opens at once and without animating, so reading along a row of icons is quick.

parts.Provider: Shares the timing between the tooltips inside it: `delay` before the first opens, 500ms by default, and none for the next while one is showing.
parts.Trigger: What the tooltip is about. It is a button unless `render` draws it as something else, such as a `Button`.
parts.Content: The hint, in a layer over the page. `variant` picks the look and `side` the side of the trigger it opens on; it moves to the other side where there is no room. `arrow={false}` takes the arrow off.
parts.Title: A heavier first line, for the `rich` look.
parts.Shortcut: The keys for the action, as key caps at the end of the line. It only shows them; handle the keys where the action lives.

examples.title: Solid
examples.description: The default: a small pill in the inverse of the page. Use it to name the buttons in a row of icons. Move along the row and each one opens at once.

examples.title: Outline
examples.description: The popover surface with a hairline edge. It sits more quietly beside a form than a dark pill, which suits a line of help next to a label.

examples.title: Shortcut
examples.description: The name and its keys side by side on a frosted chip, for the tools of an editor. It has no arrow, so a row of them opened one after another reads as one strip.

examples.title: Rich
examples.description: A small card with a `Tooltip.Title` and a `Tooltip.Description`, for saying what a control will do before it is pressed. Keep it to two or three lines.

examples.title: Tone
examples.description: `variant="tone"` tints it in a status colour with a dot. `tone` is `info`, `success`, `warning` or `destructive`. Use it for a hint that warns or confirms, such as what a delete will remove.

examples.title: Sides
examples.description: `side` picks the side of the trigger it opens on: `top`, `right`, `bottom` or `left`. Where there is no room on that side, it opens on the opposite one. `align` lines it up along the side, at its `start`, `center` or `end`.

examples.title: Following the pointer
examples.description: `trackCursorAxis="x"` on the root keeps the tooltip over the pointer as it moves along the trigger, for reading values off a chart. The trigger here is the whole chart, and the content changes with the bar under the pointer.

notes:
### Accessibility

A tooltip is for people who can see it. A screen reader does not read it, so the trigger must carry the same words in its own name: give an icon button an `aria-label` that matches its tooltip, as every example here does.

The tooltip opens when the trigger is focused from the keyboard and closes on Escape.

### Reduced motion

With reduced motion turned on, it appears and goes without growing or fading.
